meta.title: SiteSeer for industry: the building, at every stage
meta.description: One 3D model of the building at every stage, for RFIs, defects, limitations and inductions.

hero.statement: The building in 3D at every stage, from footings to fit-out. Raise RFIs, trace defects and record limitations against the exact element, before and during construction.

steps.line: Find the detail in seconds, at the stage it matters.
Raise an RFI against the exact element.

inspect.title: Lintel bearing
inspect.text: Confirm the minimum bearing each side of the opening for the paired angle lintel.

inspect.title: Weep holes over the head
inspect.text: Weep holes in the course above the lintel, at the same spacing as the base course.

steps.line: Walk a defect back to where it started.

pulls.title: Cavity tray lap
pulls.text: With the veneer pulled back, check the tray flashing laps and drains to the weep holes.

pulls.title: Head flashing
pulls.text: Recorded against the layer: the head detail relies on the flashing, not the sealant.

steps.line: The whole site, before anyone sets foot on it.

problem.heading: Drawings don't show the sequence.
problem.lede: Questions about a detail usually arrive as a marked-up PDF and an email thread, after the moment they mattered. SiteSeer puts the building, at every stage, in front of everyone who needs to see it.

points.title: RFIs without the back-and-forth.
points.text: Point at the element itself, at the stage it is built, instead of describing it.

points.title: Defects found while they're cheap.
points.text: Step back through the build to see what was covered up, and when.

points.title: Limitations written down.
points.text: Record what a detail can't do against the model, where the next person will find it.

problem.alt: A bolted steel knee connection where a portal frame rafter meets its column
problem.caption: A portal frame connection, bolted as it is fabricated.

how.heading: Pause the build. Walk in.
how.lede: Pick a stage and step inside it. Try the buttons on the wall: this is the same idea, on a whole building.

points.title: Pick a stage.
points.text: Footings, frame, lock-up or fit-out. The building waits at that point while you look around it.

points.title: Peel back the layers.
points.text: Turn layers on and off to see the frame, the cavity and the flashings behind the finish.

points.title: Pin it to the element.
points.text: Questions, defects and notes sit on the model, at the stage they belong to.

strip.alt: A timber wall frame standing on a slab beside a site workbench
strip.caption: The frame, before the lining goes on.

strip.alt: A raking-ceiling room with blue sarking and insulation exposed between the framing
strip.caption: Sarking and insulation, before they're covered.

strip.alt: A two-storey house mid-construction on a suburban site
strip.caption: The whole house, part way through the build.

uses.heading: One model for the questions a site raises.
uses.lede: Everyone looks at the same element, at the same stage.

items.title: Ask about the exact element.
items.text: Pin a question to the element at the stage it is built, so everyone answers the same thing.

items.title: Trace it back.
items.text: Walk a defect back through the stages to where it started, and what covered it up.

items.title: Write down what it can't do.
items.text: Record a detail's limits against the model, where the next trade will see them.

items.title: Walk the site before day one.
items.text: Take new crews through the site and its hazards before they arrive.

access.heading: In the office and on site.
access.lede: On the machines your team already has, at the desk and at the slab edge.

ways.title: In the office
ways.text: Runs on the Windows and macOS machines your team already uses.

ways.title: On site
ways.text: Open it on a tablet or phone at the slab edge.

ways.title: In the browser
ways.text: Share a model with the browser viewer, with nothing to install.

ways.title: Training rooms
ways.text: Deploy the Unreal Engine build to training-room computers for inductions.

results.heading: A decade of explaining buildings.
results.lede: SiteSeer began in construction education, where a building has to make sense to someone who has never seen it built. That's what a site team needs too.

outcomes.title: Shared understanding.
outcomes.text: Everyone looks at the same element at the same stage.

outcomes.title: Earlier answers.
outcomes.text: Questions are raised against the model before the trade arrives.

outcomes.title: A record that stays.
outcomes.text: RFIs, defects and limitations stay with the model after handover.

contact.heading: See it on your build.
contact.lede: Book a walkthrough, or talk to us about piloting SiteSeer on a live project.

upcoming.heading: Upcoming features.
upcoming.intro: SiteSeer is continuously evolving. These are the features we're building for project teams.
